mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops below 5% but S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is low and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is high, it indicates a potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the specified conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the next 60 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) during a late-cycle expansion indicates potential supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 1% in the last month
failure_condition: If INDPRO grows but S&P 500 returns remain positive, indicating no supply constraints.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which may increase liquidity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains low but S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: If RSAFS grows but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 5 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) increases and unemployment (UNRATE) decreases, it indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the specified conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary tightening cycle may lead to decreased liquidity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is high but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the next 60 trading days.
